fields.title: Setting targets based on distribution
fields.keyTakeaway: A speed target consists of a percentile, a threshold, and load conditions, and the threshold comes from human perception rather than current system capabilities.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: What number should we set as the target: "response time under 500 ms" refers to which percentile?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: A goal without a percentile is unachievable by definition: there will always be a request slower than any threshold. Such a goal is either ignored or generates endless tail optimization.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: A proper formulation always contains three parts: **percentile, threshold, and conditions.**
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: "p95 catalog open response time does not exceed 800 ms under loads up to 500 RPS."
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: *p50*—to understand the typical experience. As a target, it is almost useless: improving the median does not help those having a bad experience. *p95*—the working target for most scenarios. Achievable and covers the vast majority. *p99*—for critical scenarios and where requests per session are high. *p99.9*—rarely, usually for infrastructure components.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: How to choose a threshold—based on perception, not capabilities:
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/rows/2/1: Noticeable pause, but flow is unbroken
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: This same table explains why improving from 4 seconds to 2 is more valuable than from 400 ms to 200: the former moves you across categories, while the latter does not.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Separately: **different screens deserve different targets.** Opening the main screen must be fast because it is the first impression. Generating an annual report can take a minute if you warn the user.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/rows/0/1: p95 <= 1.5 s at up to 500 RPS load
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: Adding to cart is the only scenario with a p99 target, and the reason is frequency: a person adds 8–12 items per session. At p95 = 300 ms, they have about a 45% chance of encountering a slow addition at least once. Here the tail matters more than the median.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Checkout has two targets because p99 is determined by the provider and we cannot improve it—but we must know and monitor it.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: A response time target does not cover perceived speed: a screen can respond in 200 ms and still feel slow due to animations and rendering order.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: A speed target consists of a percentile, a threshold, and load conditions, and the threshold comes from human perception rather than current system capabilities.
